outcome: admissions to Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU)
cohort: Asymptomatic women with twin pregnancies and a short cervix (<= 25 mm) at transvaginal ultrasound examination during the second trimester who received either an ultrasound-indicated cerclage or a cervical pessary.
finding: Ultrasound-indicated cerclage was associated with a lower rate of preterm birth before 34 weeks of gestation and reduced composite adverse neonatal outcomes compared to cervical pessary in asymptomatic twin pregnancies with a short cervix.
gest_age: Second trimester (for intervention selection); outcomes measured for preterm birth <28, <32, <34 weeks gestation; median gestational age at delivery reported.
